harrisonTag.label: Your Harrison deer hunt: licence and tag

hits.label: Mule kick, then a hard low run

waits.text: Rifle a few minutes, bow 15 to 30 minutes

hits.note: Sources agree on a short wait, about 30 minutes (70%). A rifle hit in the heart or lungs: the deer is usually dead within 137 m (150 yd) (70%, NDA 2012).

hits.label: Dropped on the spot
hits.means: Spine or brain. It may get up. Be ready

waits.text: Watch for 5 minutes in case it stands

hits.note: Reload, safety on, scope on it. Spine shock can wear off in about a minute (85%, Grandpa: down is not dead). Heart or lungs and it went down in sight: go when it stops moving (Tip).

hits.label: Hunched back, short run, then a walk

waits.text: 6 to 8 hours, or overnight if late

hits.note: Every source says hours, and gut is the longest wait (70%). Warm afternoon and a gut hit: the meat clock and the waiting clock fight (Tip).

hits.label: Hard run with a limp

waits.text: Leg or bone: track at once

hits.note: NDA 2012 gives no wait for a leg hit (70%).

hits.label: Dark red blood, no bubbles
hits.means: Often the liver (blood sign at the hit site)
hits.note: Every source says hours, longer than for a lung hit (70%).

hits.label: No clear reaction, or I am not sure
hits.means: Not proof of a miss. Check the hit site later

waits.text: Count down from the gut wait: 10 to 12 hours

hits.note: Not sure where it hit: wait as for a gut hit is the safe reading (Tip).

callYourWait: Your call. The sources disagree on liver and gut. The app shows them all and picks none (lesson: Wait times by hit type). Opinion, not law.

steps.title: Mark the spot
steps.why: Tip: the first minutes after the shot decide most recoveries. A pin and a landmark give you a line to follow.
do: Rifle reloaded and on safe. Keep watching where it went. Listen for a crash (Tip).
Tap Save my spot above: it pins where you shot from.
Note a landmark at the last place you saw it: a tree, a rock, a stump (Tip).
tips: Drop a phone map pin where you shot from and where the deer stood. Note the time. Tip, from the After the shot lesson.
Flags you can see from the last flag show the line of travel. Tip, from the Blood trailing lesson.

steps.title: What did you see?
steps.why: The reaction to the hit tells you how long to wait. Walk in too soon and you push a hit deer out of the country.

rules.t: Following the trail of wildlife while you have a firearm is hunting.
No hunting game from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise.

tips: Reactions are hunter education advice (70%), not law.
Rain or snow coming: go sooner. Rain erases blood in an hour. Tip.

steps.title: Track it
steps.why: Slow and beside the line finds deer. Fast and on the line loses them.
do: Go to where it stood. Look for blood, hair, scuffed ground (Tip).
Flag every blood spot with tape or toilet paper. Collect the tape after (Tip).
Walk beside the blood line, not on it (70%, BC Outdoors Magazine).
Look ahead for the deer, not only down at blood (Tip).
Lost it? Back to the last flag. Circles at 20 m and 40 m, then lanes about 10 m apart, each person in sight of the next (70%, NDA, National Deer Association).

rules.t: You must make all reasonable effort to locate, dispatch, retrieve and include a wounded animal in your bag limit.
No hunting with a light. Tracking with your rifle and a headlamp after legal hours is hunting outside hours and with a light. Do not.
rules.p: page 11 (hours and lights); my reading in the Blood trailing lesson

rules.t: The trail goes into fenced or posted private land: stop. The Trespass Act has no tracking exception. Get the owner's permission, in writing if you can.
Dogs used on deer must be on a leash.

tips: Wounded deer often head downhill and to water (70%, NDA).
Hydrogen peroxide fizzes on blood you cannot see in leaves (70%, NDA).
Lost the light on a sure lung hit? Call RAPP (Report All Poachers and Polluters), 1 877 952 7277, and ask for direction (lesson lean). Doubtful hit: back out until legal light.
Nothing found: come back at first light. Ravens show you. Tip.

steps.title: Approach and confirm
steps.why: A deer that drops can get up. Approach ready, and check it is dead before anything else.
do: Come in from behind its back, rifle ready (Tip).
Touch the eye with a stick. No blink: dead (Tip).
Alive and bedded? Only if it is legal hours and the backstop is safe, finish it. If not, back out again (Tip).
Do not handle it yet. The licence comes first (next step).

rules.t: You cannot shoot a wounded animal after legal hours. No exception.
Cancel the species licence immediately after the kill and before you handle the animal.

tips: Spine shock can wear off in about a minute (85%, Grandpa: down is not dead).
Pin where the deer lies (button below). Your map waypoint and the meat plan start here.

steps.title: Cancel the licence
steps.why: A deer with no properly cancelled licence is an illegal deer, even if you did everything else right.
steps.law: "Any person who kills any big game species must immediately after the kill and before handling the big game killed, cancel the appropriate species licence in accordance with the instructions on that licence."
checks: Animal down. Do not touch it yet.
Take out the species licence for it (your own deer licence, never your partner's).
Cancel it as the licence itself shows: notch it.
Now you may handle the animal.
Keep the cancelled licence with the meat.

checksSrc.p: Rule Book: Cancelling your species licence (5 steps), page 11

rules.t: How to cancel is printed on the species licence itself, not in the synopsis. Follow what is printed on yours.
You must notch your species licence to cancel it as soon as you harvest an animal.
A cancelled licence records the date, the region number and, where it applies, the antler configuration. Harrison is Region 2.
rules.p: species licences page; region from the Harrison lesson

rules.t: Possessing a big game animal without a properly cancelled species licence is unlawful.
Each hunter cancels only their own licence, for their own kill. Never use another person's licence.
Carry all your species licences while hunting, cancelled and uncancelled.
Killed the wrong animal? Cancel at once, write in ink on the licence that you intend to self report, and call RAPP (Report All Poachers and Polluters), 1 877 952 7277.

tips: Cut cleanly with a knife or scissors. Make the notch obvious. Tip.
Carry a pen. Some fields may be written, not cut. VERIFY on your own licence before the hunt.
Photo the notched licence beside the deer (next step). Tip.

steps.title: Photos and notes
steps.why: Photos and a few notes now prove the cancelled licence, help the butcher, and teach you for next time.
do: Photo 2: the notched licence beside the deer.
Photo 3: the spot, with the landmark.
tips: Take photos: the deer, the notched licence, the spot. Tip, from the After the shot lesson.
At home: log the date, region, MU (Management Unit) and species in your journal. Tip, from the Rule Book.

steps.title: Field dress
steps.why: Meat starts to spoil the minute the heart stops. The next hour with a knife decides what ends up in your freezer.

before.t: Plan which hind quarter keeps the unskinned tail and the testicle (buck) or udder (doe). Cut around them, never through them.
Rifle unloaded and set where it will not fall or get blood in the action.
Bear spray on your belt, not in the pack.
Gloves on. Do not cut the stomach or guts.

methods.label: Gutted (whole deer, near the truck)
steps: On its back, head uphill, gloves on.
Belly cut, blade edge up, fingers guiding.
Diaphragm, then windpipe. Pull it all out.
methods.src: After the shot lesson, 4 key steps (Tip)

methods.label: Gutless (deer far from the truck)
steps: Cut around the knees, legs and belly line. Leave the sex parts attached.
Skin the top half back. The hide is your mat.
Front quarter off through the armpit.
Hind quarter off at the hip joint.
Tenderloin from inside, behind the last rib.
Bag every piece. Flip and repeat.
methods.src: Field dressing lesson, 8 steps (80%, Alaska Department of Fish and Game)

steps.lean: Lesson lean (Tip): deer within 300 m of the truck or ATV (all terrain vehicle): gut it and drag or carry it whole. A kilometre into the timber: gutless, into bags, pack it out.

rules.t: Deer evidence of sex stays naturally attached: the unskinned tail AND, for a buck, a testicle or part of the penis; for a doe, part of the udder and teats.
Antlers are not on the deer list. Keep the tail and sex parts even on a buck.
Take all the edible portions: neck, ribs, four quarters and the loins. Gutless does not excuse you.
Boned meat: leave the unskinned tail and the sex parts naturally attached to one piece. Keep that piece with the rest, labelled.
A carcass or gut pile is a wildlife attractant. Never leave one where people are, or are likely to be.

bear.t: One works and talks, one watches. Make noise while you dress it.
Get the meat out fast. Avoid dressing at dusk if you can.
Leaving meat? Move it at least 200 m from the gut pile. Hang it 3.5 m (11.5 ft) up and 1.5 m (5 ft) from trunks, where you can see it from a distance.
Coming back: approach from upwind, glass it first, make noise. Bear at the site, or the carcass moved or buried? Do not approach. Leave and report.
Do not drag the carcass back to camp: it lays a scent trail to you.
Aggressive bear or a kill site near people: call RAPP (Report All Poachers and Polluters), 1 877 952 7277, 24 hours.

tips: If gut contents touch meat, wipe them off right away with a clean cloth (75%, Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife).
Never leave the guts in overnight and come back: it spoils regardless of temperature (80%, Alaska Department of Fish and Game).

steps.title: Cool the meat
steps.why: Nobody loses meat to a bad shot. They lose it to a warm afternoon, a tarp and a closed truck.

numbers.t: Target for the carcass, as fast as you can. Slows bacteria, does not kill them.
The danger zone. Bacteria can double every 20 minutes.
Guts out or meat off. The cavity is the hottest part and stays hot.
Ideally into a cooler on the day of the kill.
Aging range, 7 to 14 days at most.
Freezer. Game keeps about a year.
Minimum internal cooking temperature for all wild game.
numbers.p: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, in the Meat care lesson

do.t: Prop the chest open so air moves. Hang it, or lay it on logs, off the ground.
Above 4°C: bags of ice or snow in the cavity, tied shut.
No plastic, no tarp on a warm carcass. "Plastic will hold heat in."
Flies: game bags. Black pepper or food grade citric acid on the surface helps.
Rain: a tarp as a roof above, with an air gap. Never wrapped around.

tips: Wet meat spoils faster. Dry it with paper towel and keep it in bags under cover. Tip.
Warm day plan: skin, quarter, bag, shade by noon. Cooler by evening. Tip.
Never let a warm deer sit in a closed truck. Grandpa's rule (opinion).

steps.title: Papers and transport
steps.why: A legal kill can still become an illegal deer in the truck: the wrong part cut off, the wrong paper.
checks: My cancelled species licence travels with the meat.
Tail unskinned and evidence of sex still attached.
Rifle unloaded in the truck: chamber and attached magazine empty.
All edible portions packed: neck, ribs, four quarters, loins.
No gut pile left near a road, trail or campsite.

rules.t: Your own deer: carry the species licence it was taken under with the meat.
Anyone moving your deer without you (your brother, a friend) needs a Record of Receipt from you.

Record of Receipt shows: date and place of receipt; name and address of the hunter; name and address of who it goes to; the hunter's FWID (Fish and Wildlife ID) or permit number; the species licence number; the species and sex.
Evidence of sex may come off only: at home once butchered and stored there; at a meat cutter or cold storage plant; or after a compulsory inspector has inspected it.
No loaded firearm in or on a vehicle: chamber and attached magazine empty.
At the butcher: get a receipt showing the hunter's FWID (Fish and Wildlife ID), the species licence number, and the species and sex.
A meat cutter records the MU (Management Unit) where the deer was taken. Know your MU before you drop it off.
rules.p: page 14; my reading in the Rule Book

report.t: Deer are not on the compulsory inspection or compulsory reporting lists. No report, no inspection trip for your Harrison deer.
In Region 2, compulsory inspection is for mountain goat and cougar, not deer.
Mandatory hunter reports cover elk, moose and caribou licences, not deer.
Chronic Wasting Disease carcass rules apply only to kills in the Kootenay zone, MUs 4-1 to 4-8 and 4-20 to 4-25. Harrison (Region 2) is outside it.

report.p: page 15 (Rule Book: disposal and game checks)

ror: Hunter FWID (Fish and Wildlife ID) number
tips: Write the Record of Receipt on paper the moment meat changes hands, and photograph it. Tip, from the Rule Book.
At the truck: tail on, evidence of sex on, cancelled licence in the cooler bag with the meat. Tip, from the Rule Book.

steps.why: Write it down tonight. One lesson from today is worth ten from a book.
tips: Write it in your journal tonight. Tip.
